atPeriodEnd: At the end of this period
atRiskRenewalsHint: Trials converting, or a card that failed
autoReactivate: Restore access the moment the invoice is paid
autoSuspend: Suspend automatically at the end of the grace period
cancelAtPeriodEnd: At the end of the paid period
changePlanHint: At period end keeps what they already paid for. Now prorates the difference onto the next invoice.
chasingEnabledHint: Off: nothing is sent or suspended; the overdue list still shows who owes.
chasingOffNote: While it is off, the overdue list tells the team what to do by these same days: remind, send the final notice, then suspend.
collectionRateHint: Of last month's renewals, without a reminder
errAfterSuspend: Retries and reminders have to come before day {{day}}, when access is suspended.
errDays: Days are whole numbers from 0 to 90, separated by commas.
errFinalAfterGrace: The final notice has to go out before access is suspended.
errFinalGraceRange: Final notice day is 1–89 and the grace period 2–90 days.
errTemplate: None of the three messages can be empty.
extendHint: Moves the period end without an invoice. A past-due client goes back to active for the days given.
extendReasonPlaceholder: Install was late, goodwill after outage…
extraDaysInvalid: Enter a whole number of days from 1 to {{max}}.
includePayLink: Include a Click / Payme link that pays the invoice in two taps
invoicesSubtitle: Every invoice issued to every client
linkHint: {{link}} becomes a Click / Payme link for this invoice.
linkOffNote: The pay link is off, so {{link}} is left empty.
mrrHint: Yearly plans counted at a twelfth
mrrTrendHint: New and churned revenue under the line
nobodyOverdueHint: Every open invoice is still inside its due date.
noteBankRef: Bank reference, who brought the cash…
offerDefault: Assalomu alaykum, {{name}}! {{business}} uchun Octopos'ga qaytsangiz, 3 oy davomida 30% chegirma beramiz. Yangi imkoniyatlar: fiskal cheklar va valyuta kurslari. Javob yozing — o'zimiz sozlab beramiz.
offerHint: The discount applies from the first invoice after they come back, for the months you choose.
overdueHintSettings: Oldest first. Each account follows the payment chasing schedule; a promise to pay pauses it until the promised day.
overdueSubtitle: The dunning queue: remind, final notice, suspend
paymentChasingHint: What happens on its own when an invoice goes unpaid. Retry the card a few times, remind people who pay by hand, warn once more, and only then suspend — never on the first failure.
paymentChasingSubtitle: Retries, reminders, grace period and messages — what runs on its own
paymentsHint: Failed charges stay here with the provider's reason, so a call can start with it.
paymentsSubtitle: Click, Payme and manual payments, failed ones included
plansHint: Prices and features are defined in the API's billing/plan package; this is what clients are on today.
plansSubtitle: Prices, features and who is on each
promiseBroken: Promise broken: {{amount}} was due by {{date}}. Reminders resumed.

promiseNotePlaceholder: Who promised, how they will pay…
readyToSuspendDays: Over {{days}} days past due, final notice sent
recordPaymentHint: For money that arrived outside Click and Payme — a bank transfer or cash. {{number}}, {{due}} due.
remindAllHint: Each gets the reminder template with their own name, amount and pay link. Accounts with a promise to pay are not listed.
renewalsHint: Autopay clients need watching only when a card fails. Everyone else needs a reminder before the day.
renewalsSubtitle: Who pays next, and who will need a nudge
retryDaysHint: Autopay clients only. Hard declines (stolen, closed card) stop the retries.
suspendedUnpaidHint: Automatically, {{days}} days past due and after the final notice
voidHint: The client no longer owes it. A voided invoice stays in the history and cannot be reopened.
winBackCall: Call {{name}} — what would bring them back?
winBackHint: Clients who left recently, newest first. The first weeks after leaving are when an offer works — before the new system is settled in.
winBackSubtitle: Clients who left recently, why, and an offer to return
